verdicts.corrected_rule: Duplicate occurrences of the same option are allowed and the LAST occurrence's value is what the program stores and uses; no warning is printed and stderr is empty. However RC=0 is not guaranteed: each occurrence is type-converted at the moment it is parsed, so an invalid int in ANY occurrence of --f/--g (or a bare trailing occurrence with no value) aborts with RC=2 and the usual `argument --X: invalid int value: '<v>'` / `argument --X: expected one argument` message, even when the last occurrence is valid. Conversely, only the surviving last value reaches base58, so an invalid base58 string in a non-last --b/--e occurrence is harmless while one in the last occurrence produces RC=1 and the PyInstaller unhandled-exception line on stderr.
